subject: Deployment mode tradeoffs & PoC commitments — next steps
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kline <sarah.k@brightmed.ai>, Alex Turner <procurement@brightmed.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + proposed PoC path (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Short recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can lock the PoC path: 

Call notes (high level):
- BrightMed wants to validate LLM-driven patient triage and note summarization in a controlled environment.
- Primary constraint: PHI handling and SOC2/audit requirements — procurement flagged data residency and audit logs.
- Technical appetite: dev team prefers minimal infra overhead but will accept short-term Dedicated capacity if it shortens time-to-impact. Security team leaning toward Private VPC for production.

Proposed PoC approach (two parallel options to keep momentum):
1) Fast-track Hosted API trial (2 weeks): quick integration for functional validation, but stays behind a privacy boundary — not suitable for PHI production. Success criteria: integration validates inference latency (<300ms p95 for short prompts), 90% of sample summaries pass quality baseline.
2) Private-VPC proof (4–6 weeks): parallel setup to validate security posture, KMS integration, and audit log shipping. Success criteria: VN in VPC with end-to-end encryption, KMS key import test, audit logs to SIEM, and sample throughput targets.

Who to own what:
- BrightMed: Sarah (clinical product) for acceptance criteria, Alex (procurement) for security/compliance gating.
- Redwood: Marissa (solutions) to lead PoC ops; Ben (infra) to coordinate Dedicated vs Private provisioning and timeline. I will coordinate exec alignment and commercial ask.

Immediate asks:
- Can you confirm which of the two PoC tracks you want to prioritize? If Private-VPC, confirm network lead and preferred window (we suggested 5/26 start).
- Alex — can you share the specialized security questionnaire? we can pre-populate answers for common items.

Attachments: PoC outline (draft) — I attached an outline you can review for scope and timeline.

Thanks,

Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
nikhil@redwood.com

From: Sarah Kline <sarah.k@brightmed.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Turner <procurement@brightmed.ai>
Date: 2025-05-14T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed PoC path (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Thanks, Nikhil — helpful summary. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

1) Security posture: Production must be Private VPC or on-prem equivalent. For the PoC we are open to a Private-VPC sandbox — procurement wants to see network isolation, KMS integration, and SYSLOG export to our Splunk instance. Hosted API is fine for initial model quality checks but we will not put PHI there.

2) Timeline: Security team prefers a 4-week window for review and initial validation. The earliest start we can commit to is the week of 5/26.

3) Success criteria (clinical):
- Summaries must not hallucinate medication details in >95% of sample cases.
- Average summary F1 vs clinician baseline >= 0.78 on our annotated set.

4) Stakeholders:
- Clinical product: Sarah Kline (me)
- Security/compliance: Alex Turner (procurement)
- Network lead: Priya Menon (cc not included here; will introduce after we decide PoC track)

Alex — I'll upload the vendor questionnaire in the next email (we have a slightly different format than the stub).

Best,
Sarah
Chief Product Officer, BrightMed

Subject: PoC playbook + technical checklist for Private-VPC track

Hi Sarah — looping in from solutions/infra to propose a tight PoC playbook that matches your asks. I tried to minimize friction while covering the compliance gates.

Summary of proposed PoC (Private-VPC sandbox):
- Duration: 4 weeks (kick week of 5/26).
- Scope: model endpoint in customer VPC (Redwood-managed runtime), KMS customer key, SYSLOG export to BrightMed Splunk, sample dataset run for 2k anonymized notes, and QA evaluation pipeline.
- Deliverables:
  • Environment demo (day 7) — network reachability, KMS demo.
  • Runbook & audit logs sample (day 14) — show logs + token-level cost estimates.
  • Clinical QA report (day 28) — F1, hallucination checks, latency and throughput.

Technical checklist (items we need from BrightMed):
- VPC peering/VPN setup details or temporary bastion rules
- KMS key ARN and permissions for Redwood service account
- Splunk endpoint and ingestion key for syslog (or S3 if preferred)
- Sample data subset (anonymized) and the clinical evaluation rubric

Commercial / resource notes:
- Cost profile: Private-VPC PoC uses dedicated GPU capacity during the test window; we can provide a discounted trial rate contingent on mutual success criteria. I'll share a simple cost-estimate matrix once network requirements are finalized.

Next steps — short checklist: 
1) BrightMed confirms PoC track (Private-VPC) and provides network lead contact (Priya).
2) Alex uploads security questionnaire (we will pre-fill and return within 48 hours).
3) Redwood schedules kick and reserves capacity for week of 5/26.

If this aligns, we will convert the draft PoC_Outline into a formal MOP and calendar invites.

Thanks — Marissa
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
